title: KV cache model onboarding: sampled sequence-tail signatures, pinning hysteresis, and publish workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an onboarding flow to capture per-model KV cache characteristics focusing on tail-heavy sequence distributions. Deliverables: a lightweight sampled-sequence collector (longseq-sampler), sequence-tail signature extraction, automated pinning recommendation with hysteresis, and a publish pipeline that generates a stable profile artifact for runtime use. This ticket covers the engineering work to wire the sampler into the model onboarding pipeline, run deterministic microbenchmarks, and validate pin policies via canary traffic. Goal is to reduce tail latency and KV miss amplification for long-context workloads without regressing short-context performance.
acceptance_criteria: longseq-sampler integrated into onboarding pipeline and producing per-model sample manifests
sequence-tail signature computed for each model variant and stored as profile fields (median, 95th, tail-cluster identifiers)
pin recommendation algorithm outputs a pinned-variant key and a recommended hysteresis window
publish pipeline writes immutable profile artifact to profiles-store with version metadata and release tag
runtime picks up profile artifact and applies pin at canary traffic level; telemetry shows KV hit-rate increase for >1024 token sequences in canary
documentation and runbook updated for oncall to roll back pinning decisions
tasks: Build longseq-sampler service: sample N sequences per model from synthetic + telemetry sources
Implement tail-signature extractor: cluster tails, compute quantiles, and derive tail-categories
Design pinning-hysteresis logic: min-eval-period, performance delta threshold, forced-unpin TTL
Integrate profile publishing into CI: sign, store, and index by model+variant+runtime-kernel
Add runtime guard: canary rollout policy and automatic rollback on SLO regression
Create dashboards: seq-length vs kv-hit-rate heatmap and per-variant latency curves
Run onboarding for 6 curated open models and collect baseline data
updates: 2026-02-20: Initial ticket opened with scope and success metrics (creator: Aisha).

2026-02-24: Spike completed for longseq-sampler prototype. Collected 10k sampled sequences from hosted API logs; added synthetic sampler to cover extreme tails (Marco). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/KV/longseq-sampler-spike

2026-02-27: Design review with runtime and observability teams. Decision to compute tail signatures offline and ship immutable profile artifacts to simplify runtime lookup (notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/KV/Tail-Signature-Design).

2026-03-02: Implemented initial tail-signature extractor. Early results show two dominant tail clusters for code-oriented models and one broad tail for conversational models. Added cluster IDs to profile schema. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/832

2026-03-05: Pinning-hysteresis draft implemented. Hysteresis parameters: min_observation_window=12h, delta_threshold=8% latency reduction, forced_unpin_ttl=72h. Seeking feedback from SRE (comment from Lina S.): need telemetry hooks for rollback reasons.

2026-03-08: Canary run started for 3 models. Observed KV hit-rate uplift of 9% for sequences >2048 tokens for model-alpha; no regression for <512 tokens. Opened follow-up issue to adjust batching when pinned variant differs in quantization format. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/kv/longseq-canary-20260308
2026-03-10: Design doc updated with performance envelope and publish schema. Added acceptance criteria for immutable artifact signing. Pending review from Security/Compliance for artifact integrity.
risks: Pinned variants may use different quantization/kernels and cause unrelated latency regressions in the general pool
Sampling bias: synthetic tails might not represent real-world tails leading to suboptimal pins
Profile drift: sequence distributions shift over time requiring re-evaluation cadence
Operational complexity from multiple profile versions increasing runtime lookup overhead
decision_log: 2026-02-27: Store tail signatures as offline immutable artifacts rather than runtime-computed to reduce runtime CPU pressure (approved by runtime leads).
2026-03-01: Use hybrid sampling (10% live telemetry + 90% synthetic heavy-tail generation) to guarantee tail coverage in early onboarding (decision by profiling team).
2026-03-04: Implement hysteresis with forced_unpin TTL to avoid flip-flopping during diurnal traffic patterns (agreed in design review).
notes: Profiling harness name: longseq-sampler. Config files live under infra/profiling/longseq/.
Profile artifact schema v1 fields: model_id, variant, kernel_tag, tail_clusters, q50,q95,q99, pinned_variant, pin_confidence, created_at, signed_by
Follow-up: add regression tests that replay sampled sequences through runtime to validate KV hit/miss differences as part of CI
